newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen says Jannah oilfield brought on stream.
newsitem.headline: Yemen says Jannah oilfield brought on stream.

text.p: Yemen's Jannah oilfield was brought on stream on Monday, the official Radio Sanaa said.
"The Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh inaugurated today the oil production operation from the Jannah sector and the governorate of Shabwah and the governorate of Marib," it said.
"The production operation started today at a level of 15,000 barrels per day (bpd), which will rise to 30,000 bpd at the beginning of 1997 and then 70,000 bpd by the beginning of 1998."

The field, 485 km south of the Yemeni capital in block five, will be managed by six companies -- Exxon Corp, Hunt, Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Company, Private Limited Enterprises (a Greek-Russian joint venture), Total SA and the Yemen Company for Investment in Oil and Minerals.

An official source at Yemen's oil ministry told Reuters: "The oil is carried by a 37-km pipeline running west linking Jannah to the Marib central processing unit. From there the oil is sent to the Safer terminal on the Red Sea for export."
Jannah is a small strip of land separating the Marib governorate (former North Yemen) from Shabwa governorate (former South Yemen).
Yemen is one of the poorest countries in Arab world and is dependent on its oilfields which produce some 350,000 bpd.
